builds.name: Reference: Ranked support core
builds.goal: Reference for Rell: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ support players use most (2,278 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 62.3% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A frontline engager who breaks shields and steals defenses, clustering enemies for allied follow-up through mounting and dragging control. The current support provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Zeke's Convergence → Locket of the Iron Solari → Knight's Vow. Aftershock keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Plated Steelcaps, Celestial Opposition, Bandlepipes.
builds.summary: The proven support baseline: Zeke's Convergence → Locket of the Iron Solari → Knight's Vow, with Aftershock.
testPlan: Play it in support as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Zeke's Convergence → Locket of the Iron Solari → Knight's Vow) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 62.3% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Zeke's Convergence → Locket of the Iron Solari → Knight's Vow.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula: Rell's Attacks and Abilities steal [3]% Armor and [3]% Magic Resist for [5] seconds. Max: [15]%. Basic attacks deal [(0.05) × Stat(1) + (0.05) × Stat(6)] magic damage on-hit.

Passive - Mounted Alacrity: Rell gains @spell.RellW_Dismount:MountedMoveSpeed@ Move Speed while mounted.

Active - {{Spell_RellW_Dismount_Name}}: Rell leaps off her mount, Knocking Up enemies and dealing @spell.RellW_Dismount:DismountDamage@ magic damage. Rell gains @spell.RellW_Dismount:Shield@ Shield, which lasts until she remounts.

Rell then enters her armored form, gaining @spell.RellW_Dismount:ResistanceIncrease*100@% increased Armor and Magic Resist, @spell.RellW_Dismount:DismountedASBoost*100@% Attack Speed and @spell.RellW_Dismount:DismountedRangeBoost@ Attack Range. In this armored form, she can use {{Spell_RellW_MountUp_Name2}}.

Rell and an ally charge, gaining [15]% Move Speed, increased to [30]% when facing enemy champions or each other for [3] seconds. Rell's next Attack or {{Spell_RellQ_Name}} explodes in an area for [0.05 / 0.055 / 0.06 / 0.065 / 0.07 + (0.0003) × AP] max Health magic damage.
Rell thrusts her lance, Stunning targets for [0.65] seconds, destroying all Shields, and dealing [60 / 100 / 140 / 180 / 220 + (0.6) × AP] magic damage.

Rell explodes in a magnetic fury, violently Pulling nearby enemies towards herself. Then Rell constantly Drags nearby enemies towards herself and deals [(75 / 125 / 175 + (0.55) × AP) × (2)] magic damage over the next [2] seconds.

builds.name: Stolen-resistance attack weave
builds.summary: Explore actual attacks while dismounted to use stolen defenses offensively.
builds.goal: Explore actual attacks while dismounted to use stolen defenses offensively.
builds.hypothesis: Break the Mold steals armor/MR through attacks and abilities and attacks add 0.05 armor plus 0.05 MR magic damage. Dismounted W explicitly grants increased attack speed and defenses. Nashor and Dusk and Dawn test an attack component; Abyssal helps close magic damage and E or remount supplies access.
testPlan: Required state: W dismounted state and finite stolen-resistance stacks are recorded; attacks can reach champions.
Log stolen stats, passive damage and Dusk packets for identical dismounted attack counts.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Delayed protective items and weak attack uptime can erase this offensive support gamble.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Repeating on-hits need not repeat resistance-steal stacks; never grant unlimited theft.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Celestial Opposition, Dusk and Dawn, Nashor's Tooth, Abyssal Mask, Jak'Sho, The Protean, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Mobile bodyguard
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Rell: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A frontline engager who breaks shields and steals defenses, clustering enemies for allied follow-up through mounting and dragging control. Record shield breaking, defense stealing and actual R clustering. AP output must repay reduced support durability; allies still supply most follow-up damage. Movement, affordable protection and a later reset item test repeated rescue participation.
builds.summary: Movement, affordable protection and a later reset item test repeated rescue participation.
testPlan: Kit question for Rell: Record shield breaking, defense stealing and actual R clustering. AP output must repay reduced support durability; allies still supply most follow-up damage.

Start with the early core (Support quest, movement/boots and Locket; Warmog only after its actual threshold) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use real support income and keep the quest/vision slot.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Movement, affordable protection and a later reset item test repeated rescue participation. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Rell deals magic damage to units in a line, breaking their shields and stunning them. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Warmog is a late threshold purchase, not in-combat regeneration or an assumed early spike.

The route fails Rell's stated kit question: Record shield breaking, defense stealing and actual R clustering. AP output must repay reduced support durability; allies still supply most follow-up damage.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility. Also record allies lost while spending on personal damage.
tradeoffs: Warmog is a late threshold purchase, not in-combat regeneration or an assumed early spike.
Full cost 11,300 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Support quest, movement/boots and Locket; Warmog only after its actual threshold. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Begin with the actual support quest item; Celestial Opposition is earned by transformation, not directly bought as a 400-gold legendary. Keep buying vision.
Locket of the Iron Solari, Knight's Vow, Warmog's Armor are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Shield-break full-tilt burst
builds.summary: Use Q shield destruction before the AP-scaled max-health E explosion.
builds.goal: Use Q shield destruction before the AP-scaled max-health E explosion.
builds.hypothesis: Q destroys shields and stuns, with 0.6 AP damage. E next attack or Q explodes for max-health magic damage with an AP coefficient; R supplies two seconds of AP-scaled magic contact. Bloodletter and Liandry test sustained follow-up while Mandate requires Q/W immobilization rather than mere E speed.
testPlan: Required state: Shielded durable target; arm E and hit Q before committing R/W.
Compare Q shield removal, E explosion and R ticks at fixed target health and shields.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Failing to land Q leaves the shield intact and the expensive AP package exposed.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Shield destruction is not extra damage equal to the removed shield.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Celestial Opposition, Imperial Mandate, Liandry's Torment, Bloodletter's Curse, Zhonya's Hourglass, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
